children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the CDF, which is the probability of finding the chicken a distance of $x$ metres or less from the centre of the enclosure. $F(x)=P(X\le x)$.

answer.worked:
For $0\le x\le6$, uniform position within the enclosure gives
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\frac{\text{area of inner circle}}{\text{area of whole circle}}\\F(x)&=\frac{\pi x^2}{\pi\times6^2}\\F(x)&=\frac{x^2}{36}.\end{align*}$$
Thus $F(x)=0$ for $x<0$ and $F(x)=1$ for $x>6$.

children.prompt: Use the CDF to find the probability of finding the chicken within $6$ m of the centre of the enclosure.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(X\le6)&=F(6)\\P(X\le6)&=\frac{1}{36}(6)^2\\P(X\le6)&=1.\end{align*}$$
This makes sense because the enclosure has radius $6$ m, so the chicken must be within $6$ m of its centre.

The PDF is the derivative of the CDF. For $0<x<6$,
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=F'(x)\\f(x)&=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^2}{36}\right)\\f(x)&=\frac{x}{18}.\end{align*}$$
Hence a PDF is $f(x)=\frac{x}{18}$ for $0\le x\le6$, and $0$ otherwise.

answer.short: $P(X\le1)=\dfrac5{32}$ and $P(X>1)=\dfrac{27}{32}$. These complementary events cover all possible values of $X$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}P(X\le1)&=\frac{3}{32}\left[2x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1\\&=\frac{3}{32}\left(2-\frac13\right)\\&=\frac5{32}.\end{aligned}$$

The events are complementary, so their probabilities add to the total probability, $1$.

By symmetry about $x=2$, $P(X\ge3.5)=\dfrac{11}{256}$. The probabilities are equal.

For $0\le x\le4$,
$$\begin{aligned}F(x)&=\int_0^x\frac{3}{32}t(4-t)\,dt\\&=\frac{3}{32}\left[2t^2-\frac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^x\\&=\frac{x^2(6-x)}{32}.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
The density is symmetric about $0$, so $\mu=0$.
$$\begin{align*}E(X^2)&=\int_{-1}^1 x^2|x|\,dx\\E(X^2)&=2\int_0^1 x^3\,dx\\E(X^2)&=2\left[\frac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^1=\frac12\\\operatorname{Var}(X)&=\frac12-0^2=\frac12\\\sigma&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\\P(\mu-\sigma\le X\le\mu+\sigma)&=\int_{-1/\sqrt2}^{1/\sqrt2}|x|\,dx\\P(\mu-\sigma\le X\le\mu+\sigma)&=2\int_0^{1/\sqrt2}x\,dx\\P(\mu-\sigma\le X\le\mu+\sigma)&=\left[x^2\right]_0^{1/\sqrt2}=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Percentage $=\dfrac12\times100\%=50\%$.

For a continuous random variable, the probability of any single exact value is 0, because infinitely many values are possible in any interval.

P(a < X < b) = P(a ≤ X ≤ b)

entries.description:
The mode is the value of x at which the PDF reaches its maximum.
To find the mode, we find the PDF’s maximum turning point.
1. Differentiate f(x)
2. Solve f′(x) = 0
3. Check x is in the domain of f(x)
4. Confirm it is the global maximum using the second derivative or a gradient table, and by checking the function value at the boundaries.
For a function that is always increasing f′(x) > 0, the mode is the end of its domain.
For a function that is always decreasing f′(x) < 0, the mode is the start of its domain.

entries.description:
1. Differentiate
f(x) = (3/32)(4x − x²)
f′(x) = (3/32)(4 − 2x)
f′(x) = (3/16)(2 − x)

0 = (3/16)(2 − x)
x = 2

x = 2 is in [0,4] ✓
4. Check maximum
f″(x) = −3/16 < 0 ∴ max
f(0) = 0,   f(2) = 3/8,   f(4) = 0
∴ x = 2 is the mode.
